tools.name: get_public_org

tools.name: analyze_event_to_uef
tools.description: Turn messy live-event material (pasted festival pack, email, rundown, or notes) into a Universal Event Format (UEF) draft plus missing_fields, open_questions, and confidence. Call this when the user pasted event details and you need a structured draft before staffing or booking. Analyze only: no log

tools.name: get_uef_schema
tools.description: Return the Universal Event Format (UEF) JSON Schema for EVENT imports (schema_version 1.0), plus minimal and festival-style examples and a docs URL. Use as a schema textbook before drafting or editing UEF — no login, no AI, nothing is saved. Pair with validate_uef to check a draft locally.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: analyze_event_to_uef, get_uef_schema · Private data: get_public_org, analyze_event_to_uef, validate_uef, search_places, get_place · Public sink: analyze_event_to_uef, request_booking, request_sponsorship · Destructive: analyze_event_to_uef, get_uef_schema.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: analyze_event_to_uef, get_uef_schema · Private data: get_public_org, analyze_event_to_uef, validate_uef, search_places, get_place · Public sink: analyze_event_to_uef, request_booking, request_sponsorship · Destructive: analyze_event_to_uef, get_uef_schema

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
